key_insight: MedEvoEval tests whether doctor agents improve over time by scoring not just final diagnoses, but the actions, traces, and experience updates within and across simulated outpatient episodes.
clinical_relevance: This matters for future clinical AI because real-world utility depends on how an agent gathers evidence, uses resources, learns from prior cases, and retains safe performance over time.
method: Action-gated simulated outpatient episodes with patient, examination, and manager views
Structured traces record observations, actions, final outputs, scores, and optional write-back
Supports longitudinal evaluation of memory, transfer, update response, and retention
evidence_signal: The authors release a runnable evaluation artifact with 700 processed episodes plus schemas, runner, scoring scripts, logs, and analysis tools for episode- and step-level assessment.
watch_item: Because the framework is simulation-based and depends on episode design and scoring rules, results may not fully capture real clinical workflow complexity or deployment risks.
paper_title: MedEvoEval: Evaluating Continual Evolution of Doctor Agents through Simulated Clinical Episodes
